title: Model Validation in ASP.NET Core — Beginner to Expert
description: Implement server-side and client-side validation using ModelState, Data Annotations, custom validation attributes, and remote validation.

data.text: What Is Model Validation?

Model validation is the process of enforcing rules on the data users submit. When a user fills out a form, validation ensures each value meets your requirements — such as a required field not being empty, an email being well-formed, or a date falling within an acceptable range. When rules are broken, error messages guide the user to fix the input.

A boolean property that returns true when no validation errors are present in ModelState.
An attribute from System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations applied to model properties to declare validation rules declaratively.
Validation performed in the browser using JavaScript, providing instant feedback without a server round-trip.

data.text: ModelState: The Validation State Container

ModelState is the central object that tracks every validation error. It is populated automatically during model binding (e.g., when a string cannot be parsed to an int) and manually via AddModelError(). You check ModelState.IsValid to decide whether to process the data or redisplay the form with errors.

data.title: Manual Validation Using ModelState.AddModelError()
Model-level errors
data.text: Pass an empty string to AddModelError() to create a model-level error that applies to the entire form rather than a single field: ModelState.AddModelError("", "Your selections are inconsistent."). Display it with asp-validation-summary="ModelOnly".
Showing Validation Errors in the View
ASP.NET Core provides two tag helpers for displaying errors. Use asp-validation-summary on a <div> to show all errors in one place, and asp-validation-for on a <span> next to each individual field.

data.title: Displaying Validation Errors — Razor View

@model JobApplication @{ ViewData["Title"] = "Job Application"; }

Job Application

Male Female
@section Scripts { }

Displays only model-level errors (property errors are excluded).

data.text: Data Annotation Validation Attributes

Data annotations are attributes from System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations that declare validation rules directly on your model. ASP.NET Core automatically checks them during model binding, eliminating the need for manual checks in every action.

rows: Ensures the value is not null or empty.
Ensures a numeric value falls within a range.
Validates a string against a regex.
Ensures two properties match (e.g., password confirmation).
Validates that the value is a properly formatted email.

data.title: JobApplication Model with Data Annotations

data.text: With data annotations applied, the controller action becomes much simpler. ASP.NET Core validates all attributes automatically before the action body runs.

data.title: Simplified Controller Action Using Data Annotations

data.text: Custom Validation Attributes

When built-in attributes are not enough, you can create a custom validation attribute by inheriting from ValidationAttribute and overriding the IsValid() method. This lets you encode any business rule as a reusable attribute.

data.title: Custom Validation Attribute — FutureDateValidator
Applying the Custom Attribute on the Model
IValidatableObject for cross-field validation
data.text: For validation rules that depend on multiple properties (e.g., 'EndDate must be after StartDate'), implement IValidatableObject on your model instead of using a single attribute.
Client-Side Validation

Server-side validation is secure but slow because it requires a round-trip to the server. Client-side validation runs in the browser using jQuery Validation and jQuery Unobtrusive Validation, providing instant feedback without any server request. ASP.NET Core emits the necessary HTML5 data attributes automatically when you use validation tag helpers.

data.title: Enabling Client-Side Scripts in the Layout or View
data.code:
<!-- In _Layout.cshtml, just before closing </body> tag -->
<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.6.0.min.js"></script>
<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/jquery-validate/1.19.5/jquery.validate.min.js"></script>
<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/jquery-validation-unobtrusive/4.0.0/jquery.validate.unobtrusive.min.js"></script>

<!-- Or use the built-in partial -->
@await RenderSectionAsync("Scripts", required: false)
<partial name="_ValidationScriptsPartial" />

data.text: With these scripts loaded, the asp-validation-summary and asp-validation-for tag helpers automatically wire up client-side validation. Try submitting the job application form with an empty Name field — the error message appears immediately without a server call.

data.title: Client-side validation is not a security boundary
data.text: Client-side validation can be bypassed by disabling JavaScript or crafting raw HTTP requests. Always keep server-side validation as your authoritative check.
Remote Validation
Remote validation checks a value against the server via an asynchronous AJAX call — usually when a field loses focus. It looks like client-side validation but runs server-side code in the background.

data.title: Remote Validation for Date of Birth
Applying [Remote] on the Model Property

data.text: The [Remote] attribute takes the action method name and controller name. ASP.NET Core emits the necessary data-val-remote attributes in the HTML, and jQuery Unobtrusive calls the endpoint automatically when the DOB field loses focus.

data.text: Exercise: Apply Validation to a Registration Form

data.title: Validate a Registration Form End-to-End
data.description: Build a registration form with at least 6 fields and apply the full validation stack: data annotations, server-side ModelState checks, client-side scripts, and a remote validation for username availability.
steps: Create a RegisterViewModel with: FullName (Required, StringLength), Email (Required, EmailAddress), Password (Required, StringLength min 8), ConfirmPassword (Compare to Password), Age (Range 18–120), and Username (Required + [Remote] uniqueness check).
Build a Razor form with asp-validation-summary and asp-validation-for on each field.
Apply [Remote("CheckUsername", "Account")] on Username and create the JsonResult action.
Test invalid submissions and verify errors appear client-side instantly.
data.expectedOutcome: Empty submission shows client-side errors instantly. An already-taken username triggers a remote validation error. Valid data passes ModelState.IsValid server-side.

items.question: What is the difference between ModelState.IsValid and TryValidateModel()?
items.answer: ModelState.IsValid is a read-only check. TryValidateModel() triggers a re-validation of the model at any point in the action and returns a bool — useful after manually modifying a property.

items.question: Can I use data annotations with API controllers?
items.answer: Yes. API controllers use [ApiController] which automatically returns a 400 with validation errors when ModelState is invalid, so you rarely need to check ModelState.IsValid manually.

items.question: Why does [Required] not work on non-nullable value types like DateTime?
items.answer: A non-nullable DateTime always has a value (default is 01/01/0001), so [Required] can never fail. Use DateTime? (nullable) with [Required] instead.

items.question: Does client-side validation work with custom validation attributes?
items.answer: No, not out of the box. Custom server-side attributes do not have client-side adapters by default. You must write a custom jQuery Validation adapter or use remote validation for client-side behavior.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: ModelState tracks all validation errors from model binding and manual checks.
Use ModelState.AddModelError() for manual business-rule validation in the action.
Data annotation attributes (Required, StringLength, Range, etc.) declaratively enforce rules on model properties.
Custom validation attributes inherit from ValidationAttribute and override IsValid().
Client-side validation uses jQuery Validation and Unobtrusive Validation for instant browser feedback.
Remote validation performs server-side checks via AJAX when a field loses focus.
Client-side validation improves UX but is never a substitute for server-side validation.
data.takeaway: A robust validation strategy combines data annotations for common rules, custom attributes for business logic, and client-side scripts for a responsive user experience.
